```{r}
# packages
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(tigris)
library(ggplot2)
```

```{r}
# look at data
census <- read.csv("~/ACLU/Data_Center_Project/data/census_tracts.csv")

dc <- read.csv("~/ACLU/Data_Center_Project/data/data_center_w_census_tract.csv")

```

# Analysis

### Question 1:

**Is the share of non-white population in tracts with data centers different from the share of non-white population in tracts without data centers?** 

```{r}
# merge census data and dc data

census_merge <- census |> left_join(
  # make indicator for whether tract has dc
  dc |> mutate(data_center = 1) |> 
    select(-X, -state), 
  by = 'GEOID'
) |> 
  mutate (data_center = as.integer(!is.na(data_center)))
```

Some tracts have more than one data center facility. Therefore, the merge resulted in duplicated census rows. The next block of code de-duplicates rows with the same GEOID.

```{r}
# remove rows with duplicated GEOID (from merging in dc data where more than one data center is sited in an individual tract)

census_merge <- census_merge |> 
  distinct(GEOID, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

Next, we separate the census tracts with any data centers from the tracts without data centers.

```{r}
# tracts with data centers
tracts_w_dc <- census_merge |> 
  filter(data_center == 1)

# tracts with data centers
tracts_no_dc <- census_merge |> 
  filter(data_center == 0)
```

Calculate the non-white population share for both tract groups.

```{r}
# non-white population share for tracts with data centers

dc_nonwhite_prc <- tracts_w_dc %>%
  summarise(
    nonwhite_pct = (sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) - sum(white_nh, na.rm = TRUE)) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(nonwhite_pct)

no_dc_nonwhite_prc <- tracts_no_dc %>%
  summarise(
    nonwhite_pct = (sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) - sum(white_nh, na.rm = TRUE)) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(nonwhite_pct)

cat(
  "Non-white population share\n",
  "--------------------------\n",
  sprintf("Tracts WITH data centers: %.2f%%\n", dc_nonwhite_prc),
  sprintf("Tracts WITHOUT data centers: %.2f%%\n", no_dc_nonwhite_prc),
  sprintf("Difference: %.2f percentage points\n", dc_nonwhite_prc - no_dc_nonwhite_prc),
  sep = ""
)
```

Next, focus specifically on the black population share

```{r}
# black population share for tracts with data centers

dc_black_prc <- tracts_w_dc %>%
  summarise(
    black_pct = sum(black_nh, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(black_pct)

no_dc_black_prc <- tracts_no_dc %>%
  summarise(
    black_pct = sum(black_nh, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(black_pct)

cat(
  "Black population share\n",
  "--------------------------\n",
  sprintf("Tracts WITH data centers: %.2f%%\n", dc_black_prc),
  sprintf("Tracts WITHOUT data centers: %.2f%%\n", no_dc_black_prc),
  sprintf("Difference: %.2f percentage points\n", dc_black_prc - no_dc_black_prc),
  sep = ""
)
```

#### Focus on one state: Tennessee

```{r}
# filter for tennessee
tn_w_dc <- tracts_w_dc |> 
  filter(state == 'Tennessee')

tn_no_dc <- tracts_no_dc |> 
  filter(state == 'Tennessee')
```

```{r}
# black population share for tracts with data centers

tn_dc_black_prc <- tn_w_dc %>%
  summarise(
    black_pct = sum(black_nh, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(black_pct)

tn_no_dc_black_prc <- tn_no_dc %>%
  summarise(
    black_pct = sum(black_nh, na.rm = TRUE) / sum(total, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) |> 
  pull(black_pct)

cat(
  "Tennessee: Black population share\n",
  "--------------------------\n",
  sprintf("Tracts WITH data centers: %.2f%%\n", tn_dc_black_prc),
  sprintf("Tracts WITHOUT data centers: %.2f%%\n", tn_no_dc_black_prc),
  sprintf("Difference: %.2f percentage points\n", tn_dc_black_prc - tn_no_dc_black_prc),
  sep = ""
)
```

**State-Level Analysis**

```{r}
# function to calculate difference for all states
group_share_by_state <- function(data, group_var) {
  data |>
    group_by(state) |>
    summarise(
      n_tracts_dc     = sum(data_center == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_dc          = sum({{ group_var }}[data_center == 1], na.rm = TRUE) /
                        sum(total[data_center == 1], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      pct_no_dc       = sum({{ group_var }}[data_center == 0], na.rm = TRUE) /
                        sum(total[data_center == 0], na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(diff_pct_pts = pct_dc - pct_no_dc)
}
```

```{r}
black_by_state <- group_share_by_state(census_merge, black_nh)
black_by_state
```

Next, we can look at the top ten states for black population share differences.

```{r}
# look at top ten states for black population share differences

top10_black <- black_by_state |>
  filter(n_tracts_dc > 0) |>
  slice_max(diff_pct_pts, n = 10) |>
  mutate(across(c(pct_dc, pct_no_dc, diff_pct_pts), ~ round(.x, 1)))

top10_black

```

### Map

Starting with Tennessee, we map the Black population share by tract with facilities overlaid as points.

```{r}

# get tract boundaries for TN, using 2020 census
tn_tracts <- tracts(state = "TN", year = 2020, cb = TRUE)

tn <- census_merge |>
  filter(total > 0, state == 'Tennessee')

# join your tract-level data
tn_map <- tn_tracts |>
  left_join(
    tn |> 
      mutate(GEOID = as.character(GEOID)) |> 
      select(GEOID, pct_black_nh, data_center),
    by = "GEOID"
  )

# TO DO: using centroids but change to lat and long
fac_pts <- tn_map |>
  filter(data_center == 1) |>
  st_centroid()
```

```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = tn_map, aes(fill = pct_black_nh),
          color = "white", linewidth = 0.05) +
  geom_sf(data = fac_pts, shape = 21, fill = "red", color = "white",
          size = 2.5, stroke = 0.4) +
  scale_fill_fermenter(
    palette = "Blues", direction = 1,
    breaks = c(5, 10, 25, 50, 75),
    na.value = "grey90",
    name = "Black population\nshare (%)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Black population share and data center locations, Tennessee",
    subtitle = "Red dots mark tracts with a data center"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9, vjust = 0.8),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

```

### **Simple Logistic Regression**

Below, we run a simple logistic regression, controlling for tract population size and state fixed effects. In the future, we'd also like to control for additional factors like household income, home values, etc.

```{r}
library(fixest)

model_df <- census_merge |>
  filter(total > 0) |>
  mutate(
    black_share = black_nh / total * 100,   # percentage points
    log_pop     = log(total)
  )


# model: tract population and state fixed effects
model <- feglm(data_center ~ black_share + log_pop | state,
            data = model_df, family = binomial,
            cluster = ~state)

etable(model)
```

Nationally, there is no statistically significant relationship between a tract’s Black population share and whether it has a data center.

As an odds ratio, exp(0.0006) ≈ 1.0006. Each additional percentage point of Black population is associated with about a 0.06% change in the odds of a data center. Per 10 points, that’s roughly 0.6%.

Now we look just at Tennessee.

```{r}

# just for tennessee

tn_model_df <- census_merge |>
  filter(total > 0, state == 'Tennessee') |>
  mutate(
    black_share = black_nh / total * 100,   # percentage points
    log_pop     = log(total)
  )


# model: tract population
tn_model <- feglm(data_center ~ black_share + log_pop,
               data = tn_model_df, family = binomial,
               vcov = "hetero")

etable(tn_model)
```

In Tennessee, tracts with a higher Black population share are **significantly more likely** to have a data center, after controlling for tract population.

Per 10 points increase in a tract's Black population share: exp(0.149) ≈ 1.16; about **16% higher odds of hosting a data center.**
